after: ## A continuous spectrum with one speed (3.10)
alt: A continuous band of seven regions in order: radio waves, microwaves, infrared, visible light, ultraviolet, x-rays and gamma rays. From left to right the wavelength decreases and the frequency increases. All travel at 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s in free space, so by v = f × λ a shorter wavelength means a higher frequency.
caption: Radio to gamma: wavelength down, frequency up, same speed in free space.

alt: The visible spectrum from red at about 700 nm through orange, yellow, green, blue and indigo to violet at about 400 nm, with wavelength decreasing and frequency increasing. Infrared lies next to red and ultraviolet next to violet.
caption: Red sits next to infrared; violet sits next to ultraviolet.

alt: A radio wave of wavelength 1500 m has f = 3.0 × 10⁸ / 1500 = 2.0 × 10⁵ Hz. An x-ray of wavelength 1.0 × 10⁻¹⁰ m has f = 3.0 × 10¹⁸ Hz. The x-ray frequency is 1.5 × 10¹³ times larger because its wavelength is that many times shorter.
caption: Same speed, so f = v / λ: a far shorter wavelength gives a far higher frequency.

alt: A table of uses: radio waves for broadcasting and communications; microwaves for cooking and satellite transmissions; infrared for heaters and night vision; visible light for optical fibres and photography; ultraviolet for fluorescent lamps; x-rays for seeing internal structure; gamma rays for sterilising food and medical equipment. Each is paired with the property that makes it suitable.
caption: For each use, give the property of the radiation that makes it work.

alt: X-rays from a source pass through the soft tissue of an arm and reach a detector, but are absorbed by the denser bone. The detector records where x-rays pass and where they are stopped, giving an image of the bone.
caption: X-rays pass through soft tissue but are absorbed by bone.

alt: A table. Microwaves cause internal heating of body tissue; ovens have a metal case and door mesh and switch off when opened. Infrared causes skin burns; keep a distance and use guards and gloves. Ultraviolet damages surface cells and can cause blindness; use sunscreen, clothing, hats and UV-blocking sunglasses. Gamma rays cause cancer and mutation; use lead or concrete shielding, distance, limited time and dose badges. Higher frequency is broadly more harmful.
caption: Name the specific harm, then the measure that cuts exposure to it.
